बॉस! इस डायरेक्टर की कहानी सुनकर आपके भी रोंगटे खड़े हो जाएंगे! 🎬

नेशनल अवॉर्ड जीतने वाले डायरेक्टर विनोद कापड़ी का कहना है कि उनकी फिल्म Pyre को सिनेमाघरों तक लाना बहुत बड़ा संघर्ष था। 🎥

रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, फिल्म को इंटरनेशनल फिल्म फेस्टिवल्स में अवॉर्ड मिले, लेकिन किसी भी OTT प्लेटफॉर्म ने इसे खरीदने में दिलचस्पी नहीं दिखाई। 🚫

विनोद कापड़ी का कहना है कि वे शारीरिक, मानसिक और आर्थिक रूप से पूरी तरह टूट चुके थे, बैंक खाते में सिर्फ 7,000 रुपये बचे थे और उन्होंने टोरंटो में अवॉर्ड मिलने के बाद रिटायरमेंट का ऐलान कर दिया था। 💸

फिर एग्जीक्यूटिव प्रोड्यूसर अरिंद्र राय चौधरी ने लंदन के बिजनेसमैन सुरेश जोशी से मिलाया, जिन्होंने फिल्म के रिलीज के लिए पैसे दिए। 🤝

फिल्म ने पहले दिन 8 लाख, दूसरे दिन 27 लाख और तीसरे दिन 70 लाख रुपये की कमाई की, लेकिन एक बड़ी रिलीज Ramayana के आने के बाद उनके 70% शो कम हो गए। 📉

अब फिल्म पूरे भारत में करीब 90 शो के साथ चल रही है और सभी शो में 80% ऑक्यूपेंसी मिल रही है। ✨

क्या आपने अभी तक यह फिल्म देखी है या नहीं? नीचे कमेंट करके बताओ! 👇

ctx.title: HT Exclusive: Vinod Kapri on almost quitting filmmaking after Pyre's OTT rejection,  ₹7,000 bank balance and losing 70% shows after Ramayana release
ctx.summary: In an interview with Hindustan Times, Vinod Kapri spoke about the challenges of bringing the film Pyre to theatres.
ctx.text:
National Award-winning filmmaker Vinod Kapri says that getting Pyre to theatres was a struggle that nearly made him quit filmmaking. Despite winning awards at international film festivals, the film failed to find takers among streaming platforms and faced hurdles in securing a theatrical release. Now, with audiences responding warmly to the film, he hopes strong word of mouth will help it reach more screens. Set in Uttarakhand's Kumaon region, Pyre follows an elderly couple whose children have moved away in search of better opportunities, leaving them to face old age and loneliness together. The film stars 80-year-old Padam Singh Kapri, a retired Indian Army serviceman, and 70-year-old Heera Devi, both making their acting debuts. Padam plays a character named after himself, while Heera portrays Tulsi.
In an interview with Hindustan Times, Vinod spoke about the challenges of bringing the film to theatres, the loss of shows following the arrival of a major release and the audience response that has renewed his faith in filmmaking. He also recalled announcing his retirement after receiving an award in Toronto.
Despite the film's recognition at international festivals, finding a release platform proved to be a major challenge. Vinod said he approached several OTT platforms, but none showed interest in acquiring the film. “There are many better films than Pyre which are not released yet, which are still yet to see light of the day. There are many better films than Pyre and I know these films,” he said, pointing to the number of independent films that struggle to reach audiences despite their quality.
The experience left him physically, mentally and financially drained. Recalling how he had reached a breaking point, Vinod said, “I was so so depressed and so mentally, physically, financially exhausted that I announced my retirement from that stage after receiving the award from Deepa Meta. I said I'm done with filmmaking. I'm not going to make any film after this because I'm completely drained out after making this film.”
He credited his executive producer Arindra Rai Chaudhuri, who also came on board as a producer, for encouraging him not to lose hope. Arindra eventually connected him with London-based businessman Suresh Joshi, who watched the film and believed it deserved a theatrical release. But by then, Vinod had very little left to spend on the film. “My company bank account is only 7,000 rupees and I don't have a single penny to spend on this film anymore I don't have any energy I don't even have a money,” he recalled.
Suresh offered to put money into the release, allowing the film to reach cinemas. Vinod said he remains grateful to both for stepping in when he had almost given up on the project. Looking back, he feels the rejection from streaming platforms may have worked in the film's favour. “It is a blessing in disguise that OTT rejected this film otherwise this film could not have get this kind of love and recognition the film is getting right now,” he said.
While the film has started finding its audience, its theatrical run has not been without hurdles. Vinod said Pyre began with a limited release of around 80 screens, with the number of shows increasing as more people started watching it. “So we started with 80 screens on day one, 80 plus something, and by day five, it went up to 400 shows all over India,” he said.
He also shared how the film's opening collections grew over its first three days. “Day one we just opened with 8 lakh. Our opening was just 8 lakh rupees and on day two it went up to 27 lakhs and on day three it went up to 70,” he said.
However, the arrival of a major release Ramayana affected the film's screen count. Vinod said, “Unfortunately from last two days, our shows had been cut down by 70%. Maybe because of one big release.”
